messages.text: How England’s underdog spirit can fuel RL World Cup semi-final hopes

metadata.summary: England’s men find themselves in an unusual position: they are favourites to beat Papua New Guinea in their final group game, but underdogs to emerge from the combined Groups B and C and reach the semi-finals
metadata.content: How England must harness their underdog spirit to reach the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion How England must harness their underdog spirit to reach the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals England women face Samoa in their winner-takes-all final group game on Friday (6.45am kick-off); England men face Papua New Guinea in their final Rugby League World Cup pool fixture also on Friday (9.05am kick-off) Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Wednesday 28 October 2026 18:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brian Carney discusses the core issues surrounding Rugby League in the UK and why the gap with Australia is getting larger. England’s men find themselves in an unusual position: they are favourites to beat Papua New Guinea in their final group game, but underdogs to emerge from the combined Groups B and C and reach the semi-finals They trail Samoa by 68 points on points difference and cannot finish above Tonga because of their head-to-head record, leaving their hopes of progressing dependent on a convincing win and results elsewhere going their way. That means they must beat Papua New Guinea by as big a margin as possible, then hope Tonga defeat Samoa by enough to give England a route into the semi-finals.
